Before Dandadan, There Was Abenobashi: Remembering Anime's Forgotten Sleeper Hits

short // Jul 1, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

Do you remember when anime in the West felt like the Wild West? If you were watching anime in the late '90s and early 2000s, you know exactly what I'm talking about.

In 1995, Studio Gainax changed anime forever with Neon Genesis Evangelion. Five years later, the studio made FLCL, six episodes of pure chaotic craziness that became a cult classic. Then in 2002, the same studio did it again, and almost nobody remembers it.

The grandfathers of Western anime

We owe a massive debt to the companies that brought anime to the West back then: ADV Films, Manga Entertainment and Media Blasters. They took huge risks to bring over shows nobody was sure would sell, and they built the culture we have today.

I honestly miss the presence ADV Films had in the community. Its legacy lives on through Sentai Filmworks, which grew out of ADV and still carries the torch for physical media and dubbing. But with the shift to streaming, we're slowly losing the memory of the sleeper hits from that golden era.

Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi (2002)

Take Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi. Gainax made it in 2002 with Madhouse, and it's 13 episodes of pure chaotic energy.

Two kids from Osaka, Arumi and Sasshi, get thrown into a string of parallel worlds, and each one is a brilliant, unhinged parody of a different genre: RPGs, sci-fi epics, dating sims, film noir, kung fu cinema and more. It was scored by Shirō Sagisu, the same composer behind Evangelion, and it won an Excellence Award for animation at the Japan Media Arts Festival.

Why it's the blueprint for Dandadan

Messy kids, reality bending around them, and slapstick comedy crashing head-first into real emotion. If that formula sounds familiar, it should. It's exactly why Dandadan is such a massive hit today.

Abenobashi was pulling off that same crazy energy more than 20 years earlier. We can't let the sleeper anime that helped build the culture we love be forgotten.

Side note: it's classic early-2000s Gainax, which means it can get a little risqué. You've been warned.

Update (September 2026)

Good news for anybody who wants to track it down: while the physical releases are out of print, Abenobashi is streaming on HIDIVE, Sentai's streaming service. And Dandadan Season 3 is officially set for 2027 from Science Saru, so you've got time to catch up.

Sources: HIDIVE, Crunchyroll News, Wikipedia: Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi

Quick answers

What is Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi? A 13-episode 2002 anime from Gainax and Madhouse about two kids from Osaka who get thrown into parallel worlds that parody different genres.

Who made the music for Abenobashi? Shirō Sagisu, the composer behind Neon Genesis Evangelion.

Where can I watch Abenobashi? It's streaming on HIDIVE. The physical releases are out of print.

When does Dandadan Season 3 come out? In 2027. An exact date hasn't been announced yet.

Is Abenobashi like Dandadan? In spirit, yes: chaotic kids, reality-bending worlds, and comedy mixed with real emotion.

Your turn

What are your favorite forgotten sleeper anime from the ADV Films era? Tell me in the comments.
